comparison: Perfect alignment on FRT/FLP recombination strategy (C86-C96). Both evaluations support the technical approach, quantitative data, and verification methods. Reviewer 1 explicitly acknowledges the FLP/FRT-mediated recombination feature, confirming OpenEval's assessment of this methodology.

Complete agreement on systematic differences between LexA and QF2 systems (C120-C125). Both accept the wing pouch observations and speculative mechanistic explanations as documented limitations rather than fundamental flaws. Reviewers' overall positive assessments indicate these caveats are appropriately characterized.

Strong alignment on background and rationale (C1-C26 overlap). Both evaluations support that existing binary expression systems have documented limitations including neuronal bias and tissue specificity issues. Reviewer 2 explicitly acknowledges CNS bias in current drivers, validating the need articulated in these claims.

High concordance on expression pattern validation (C59-C64, with peer also including C127). Both evaluations support the comparability findings and documented exceptions (da and nub). Reviewers confirm thorough validation and that tissue-specific expression results were largely consistent as expected.

Strong agreement on novelty and utility of the resource (C106-C113, with peer adding C136). Both evaluations emphasize the organ system focus and scRNAseq-guided approach. Reviewers strongly endorse the significance, with explicit statements about utility for inter-organ communication studies and immediate impact on the fly community.

Good alignment on double driver strategy (C73-C85, with peer also covering C38-C40). Both support the functional validation and accept the wing pouch limitation as part of thorough characterization. Reviewer 1 explicitly notes the dual insert plasmid capability, confirming this innovative efficiency improvement.

Strong concordance on RNAi functional validation (C97-C105, with peer including C131-C133). Both evaluations support the comparative effectiveness data and phenotypic differences between systems. Reviewer 1 explicitly acknowledges the demonstration of RNAi phenotype induction, validating both the functional data and ongoing resource generation.

High agreement on marker misexpression issue and resolution (C65-C72, with peer adding C128-C130). Both evaluations accept the systematic characterization of the marker effect and its elimination through removal. Reviewers implicitly accept this as part of the thorough validation process without raising concerns.

Moderate overlap on experimental strategy and execution (C31, C36, C43, C52-C54, C56, C58). Both evaluations support the successful generation of knock-ins and verification steps. Editor and reviewers provide 'convincing evidence' statements that align with OpenEval's assessment of clear documentation and appropriate citations.

Good alignment on methodological advantages (C115-C119). Both evaluations support the efficiency claims and CRISPR methodology. Reviewer 2 explicitly praises the efficient pipeline and methodology description, confirming OpenEval's assessment of practical advantages including the 100% cloning success rate claim.

Partial overlap on design choices (C32-C33, C47). Both evaluations support the rationale for LexA-GAD over p65 and QF2 over QF. Peer reviewers accept these methodological decisions as part of well-executed methodology, though they don't explicitly discuss the specific justifications that OpenEval highlights.

Limited overlap on tissue specificity claims (C127). Both evaluations support this claim, with OpenEval linking it to Figure 2 imaging data and peer reviewers accepting it as part of the validation showing largely consistent tissue-specific expression results.

Minimal overlap on caveats and recommendations (C126). Both evaluations support the expectation of differences from GAL4 lines as reasonable inference. Peer reviewers accept this through overall positive assessment without specific challenge to comparative claims.

Partial overlap on RNAi applications (C131-C133). Both evaluations support the comparative effectiveness and ongoing resource generation. OpenEval emphasizes practical utility for RNAi, while peer reviewers focus on the demonstration of functional phenotype induction.

Limited overlap on overall contribution summary (C41-C42). Both evaluations support the shRNA evaluation and ongoing library generation. OpenEval synthesizes the scope and impact, while peer reviewers accept these as valuable systematic aspects of the work.

Minimal overlap on double driver design summary (C38-C40). Both evaluations support the experimental validation of this design feature. OpenEval includes this in overall contribution synthesis, while peer reviewers acknowledge it as part of the plasmid toolkit described.

Minimal overlap on resource contribution (C136). Both evaluations support the overall significance. OpenEval includes this in synthesis of scope and impact, while peer reviewers emphasize utility and immediate impact on the research community.

Minimal overlap on adaptability claims (C114). Both evaluations support the utility and adaptability of the resource. OpenEval emphasizes this as part of novelty assessment, while peer reviewers accept it through acknowledgment of systematic approach and value.
